incident-bot: PAGE: P1 - multiple GPU container restarts in us-west2-gpu-pool. symptom: repeated prefill OOMs during long-context loads. paging @nora (oncall).

nora (oncall): got it, joining. brief: customer-facing errors or internal only?

eli (sre): we're seeing a spike in 5xx for generation endpoints. stack traces: `CUDA out of memory` followed by SIGKILL on container. sample log:```
[2026-03-15T02:34:12Z] prefill: req_id=rc-9a3b model=gptx-70b seq_len=58000 alloc(cudaMalloc)=OOM
[2026-03-15T02:34:13Z] runtime: fatal: kernel driver warning, restarting container
```

geoff (infra): metrics show three worker nodes in the GPU pool with multiple restarts each. Pod restarts count: 7,6,5. Host GPU memory pressure high; driver messages about ECC threshold crossed. Not localized to one app — looks correlated to a set of large prefill requests from a small subset of API keys.

hana (runtime): quick analysis: streaming prefill path is not applying the streaming trim policy when a single IO chunk includes a deeply nested JSON blob (~60k tokens). The KV cache grows linearly with the token count; then allocation fails during attention map materialization. Repro: send single request with 58k tokens => deterministic OOM.

nora (oncall): mitigation options?

geoff (infra): live options: 1) cordon affected nodes and drain (may move load) 2) lift pool autoscaling (slow) 3) edge rate-limit / drop large requests at L7 (fast) 4) runtime config to enable streaming truncation + immediate soft-reject above threshold (fast) 5) temporarily route heavy traffic to CPU-quantized fallback (higher latency/cost but stable).

hana (runtime): I can flip a control-plane flag to enable stream-trim-on-prefill and set max_prefill_tokens to 24576 (24k) for this pool only. That will return a JSON error with 413 and a short explanation. I can also trigger `kv_clear` on live pods to free memory.

nora (oncall): do the 24k pool-level limit and kv_clear. also block the offending API keys/IPs at edge for 15m while we stabilize. eli, can you coordinate the edge block?

eli (sre): on it. applying WAF rules now:```
# edge controller
POST /edge/rules/apply
{ "rule": "drop", "match": { "ip_block": "203.0.113.0/28" }, "duration": "15m" }
```
Rule applied. returning 429 for matching clients.

hana (runtime): applying pool-level config:```
PATCH /v1/runtime/pools/us-west2-gpu-pool 
{ "stream_trim_on_prefill": true, "max_prefill_tokens": 24576 }
```
Config applied in ~30s. issuing soft-kill/kv-clear to the top 4 pods:```
kubectl exec -n serve gpu-pool-worker-02 -- runtime-admin kv_clear --grace 5
kubectl exec -n serve gpu-pool-worker-07 -- runtime-admin kv_clear --grace 5
kubectl delete pod gpu-pool-worker-05 -n serve --grace-period=20
```
Memory on hosts dropped quickly; restarts halted.

ops-bot: ALERT SUPPRESSION: suppressed "container_restarts" alerts for us-west2-gpu-pool for 20m (owner: nora).

sam (cust-relay): customer impact assessment: we saw a ~6% error rate bump (502/504/500) between 02:30-02:36 UTC for a handful of API keys; heavy users received 413 after our change. I've started a targeted outreach list: cust-87, cust-212, cust-opsinc. They lost a small number of requests; some had retries that succeeded after the limits.

nora (oncall): suggested short customer message: "We've applied temporary safeguards to protect stability for long-context workloads. Requests above 24k tokens will receive a 413 response while we deploy a fix. If you need assistance migrating to session-chunking or enabling session-stores, contact devex." any changes?

hana (runtime): follow-ups and actions: 1) PR to enforce KV caps and ensure stream-trim is default for streaming prefill (link in a sec) 2) add prefill token telemetry per request + alert on >90th percentile token counts 3) implement server-side per-api-key token budgeting to prevent single clients from consuming unbounded cache.

geoff (infra): I'll collect `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q` dumps and upload to the incident bucket, and schedule a kernel driver health check for the affected hosts.

nora (oncall): ownership: @geoff infra follow-up for 3h, @hana runtime bug and PR, @eli maintain edge rules and rollback in 20m if stable, @sam handle customer comms. I'll open postmortem doc and do the handoff in 2h. Leaving channel open for any regression.

incident-bot: NOTE: next oncall in 3h is @maya (oncall) 1. Added as observer.

sam (cust-relay): sending initial customer note now. scheduling phone for cust-87 (they had ~200 failed calls).

nora (oncall): thanks all. monitoring for 30m then will close. :white_check_mark:
